Hamster Corporation released the game outside Japan for the first time through their Arcade Archives series for the Nintendo Switch and PlayStation 4 in June 2021.

PC:blockland.d: Blockland is a sandbox game in which players build and play using Lego-like building blocks in singleplayer and multiplayer modes. It was created by American developer Eric "Badspot" Hartman, using the Torque Game Engine, and was originally released as freeware on November 15, 2004. The game is not endorsed by, or affiliated with, the Lego brand, but at one point, Lego was in talks with Hartman about purchasing the game. Blockland was spotlighted on The Screen Savers on February 11, 2005, drastically increasing the user base overnight.

PC:juiced.d: Juiced is a 2005 racing video game developed by British studio Juice Games for Microsoft Windows, PlayStation 2, Xbox, and mobile phones. Originally planned for release in 2004, the game was delayed to the following year, when the original publisher Acclaim Entertainment filed for bankruptcy. Juice Games and Fund 4 Games retained ownership of the property and sold the game to THQ, resulting in the new publisher funding six more months of the game's development. The game features Career and Arcade modes that offer increasingly-difficult challenges, the ability to customise both the appearance and performance of cars (including nitrous boosts), as well as unlocking new cars.
